title: Territorial Patterns of the Water–Energy–Food Nexus in the Brazilian Amazon: An Exploratory Analysis of Associations Among Agricultural Systems, Resource Use, and Vulnerabilities
content: Agroforestry systems are frequently regarded as productive alternatives capable of reconciling agricultural production and environmental conservation, yet their associations with water–energy–food (WEF) Nexus dimensions remain insufficiently explored in the Amazon. This observational and exploratory study examined territorial patterns and associations among indicators of AFS, monocultures, and municipal water, energy, and food conditions in Northern Brazil. Secondary data from 70 municipalities were analyzed using Principal Component Analysis, Pearson correlation, and linear regression with state fixed effects. The analyses were designed to identify associations rather than causal effects. The first two principal components explained 85.1% of total variance. PC1 (51.3%) was primarily defined by water and energy indicators, whereas PC2 (33.8%) was dominated by vulnerability to food insecurity. Associations between production-system indicators and Nexus components were predominantly weak. A negative and statistically significant association was observed between the log-transformed mean AFS area indicator per 1,000 rural inhabitants and PC1 (b = -0.28; p = 0.033), while the corresponding monoculture indicator was not statistically significant. The results also show that food vulnerability forms a relatively independent dimension. Overall, the findings indicate that territorial heterogeneity is an important feature of the observed WEF Nexus configuration, beyond the associations identified with production-system indicators.
